interpretation: The unit converts a reciprocal-radius threshold into an analytic-regularity threshold. Under r_n^{-1}=O(n), enough product factors at frequency |y| obey inverse-frequency bounds for Stirling's estimate to give fixed exponential decay of A(y;mu) and A(y;nu), hence F and G are real analytic; under r_n^{-1}=o(n), the exponential rate can be chosen arbitrarily large, yielding entire extensions in the two coordinate variables. The product representation gains a quantitative bridge from component scale to regularity, but compressing the factors into a decay bound does not remove the need for the product and marked-product formulas, their summability, and Fourier inversion; r_n tending to zero alone is insufficient.
source_support: Theorem 8 states real analyticity when r_n^{-1}=O(n) and entire-function regularity when r_n^{-1}=o(n). Its proof sets b=limsup r_n^{-1}/n, takes a>b so that r_n^{-1}<an eventually, allocates successive K_0 factors, applies an inverse-frequency bound, and uses Stirling to obtain exponential product decay. The displayed bound for A(y;nu) also absorbs the marked sums' polynomial factor into that decay.

The proof burden remains delegated to Theorems 13 and 14.
